title: Why Stop Signs Have Eight Sides #shorts
description:
The first stop sign is credited to Detroit in 1914, and it wasn't an octagon. In 1922 a committee of state highway officials chose the octagon, a shape no other road sign used, so drivers could recognise it quickly, even from behind. Stop signs were also yellow for decades: red-on-white signs only arrived in 1954, when fade-resistant red became practical.

Question: did you ever count the sides? Tell me in the comments.
